title: Weekly Market Outlook: Nifty snaps 8-week losing streak, but can bulls reclaim the crucial 200-week moving average?
excerpt: The Nifty snapped its eight-week losing streak but remains below the crucial 200-week moving average at 22,627. Other companies expected to launch their maiden public offerings this month include Fusion CX, HD Fire Protect, Tonbo Imaging, Bonfiglioli Transmissions, Sahajanand Medical Technologies, Paras Healthcare, NDR InvIT Trust, Gujarat Victory Forgings and SFC Environmental Technologies, according to merchant bankers.

title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: What do Shah Rukh Khan and SIFs have in common? Radhika Gupta explains
excerpt: Edelweiss Mutual Fund MD and CEO Radhika Gupta says investors should approach Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs) with clear portfolio goals rather than chase new products or returns. title: FPIs pull out ₹44,166 cr from equities in Oct, 2026 outflows cross ₹3 trn
excerpt:
Foreign investors have withdrawn Rs 44,166 crore from Indian equities so far in October, bringing the total outflows this year to more than Rs 3 lakh crore as elevated crude oil prices, a firmer US dollar and higher US bond yields weigh on investor sentiment.
Also, the artificial intelligence-led rally in North Asian markets attracts higher foreign capital.
The latest outflows follow a net withdrawal of Rs 35,861 crore in September.
Before this, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) had invested Rs 20,200 crore in Indian equities in July and Rs 29,631 crore in August, data from the NSDL showed.
With the latest selling, FPI withdrawals from Indian equities in 2026 have reached Rs 3.04 lakh…

title: PNB Housing Finance sees 5-8 bps margin improvement from rate hike: MD
excerpt:
PNB Housing Finance MD and CEO Ajai Shukla said the recent rate hike by the Reserve Bank would lead to a marginal improvement in net interest margin (NIM).
After a gap of almost four years, the Reserve Bank raised its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent, making borrowing from the central bank costlier to contain inflation fuelled by the West Asia crisis.
"Some benefit will go to the lender because all of the borrowing of the lender is not on the repo rate. It is a combination of Marginal Cost of Funds-based Lending Rate (MCLR), commercial paper, refinance from National Housing Bank and non-convertible debentures," Shukla told PTI.

title: Japan tops India's FDI chart in Q1 FY27 with $5.71 billion inflows
excerpt:
Japan has emerged as the largest source of foreign direct investment (FDI) into India during April-June of the current fiscal year, according to government data.
FDI inflows from Japan stood at USD 5.71 billion in the first quarter of 2026-27, surpassing the USD 3.74 billion India received from the country during the entire 2025-26 fiscal year. It was USD 2.48 billion in 2025-26.
The foreign inflows from Japan account for nearly 29 per cent of the total equity inflows (USD 19.81 billion) which India received during the quarter, the data showed.
